passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K (this Annual Report) and the exhibits hereto, the following risk factors should be considered carefully in evaluating our business. Our business, financial condition, cash flows or results of operations could be materially adversely affected by any of these risks. This section contains forward-looking statements. You should refer to the explanation of the qualifications and limitations on forward-looking statements set forth at the end of Part I, Item 1. Business of this Annual Report. The considerations and risks that follow are organized within relevant headings but may be relevant to other headings as well. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also adversely affect our business, financial condition, cash flows or results of operations. Economic, Industry and Geopolitical Risks We face intense competition and may not be able to keep pace with the rapid technological changes in the medical devices industry or low-cost competitive offerings, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations. The medical device markets in which we participate are highly competitive. We encounter significant competition across our product lines and in each market in which our products are sold from various medical device companies. Some of our competitors may have greater financial and marketing resources than we do, including as a result of consolidation among companies in our industry. Our primary competitors include large manufacturers with multiple lines of business and competing products, as well as a wide range of medical device companies that sell a single or limited number of competitive products or which participate in only a specific market segment or segments. We also face competition from non-medical device companies, including pharmaceutical companies, biotech companies and providers of various diagnostic solutions, which may offer alternative therapies for disease states also amenable to diagnosis or treatment using our products. New competitors may emerge in the future, potentially including companies introducing new sales or distribution models to our industry or leveraging genomic, robotic, navigation, and/or other automation technologies. Digital technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning capabilities, have and may continue to increase in their applicability and importance to various aspects of our business, operating and competitive environments, research and development (R&D) pipeline and product portfolio. We believe we will need to develop new and enhanced digital capabilities and competences in order to remain competitive. In addition, the medical device markets in which we participate are characterized by extensive research and development and rapid technological change. Developments by other companies of products and/or services, processes or technologies, including low-cost alternatives, may make our products or proposed products obsolete or less competitive and may negatively impact our net sales. credit_strengths.text: Operating income covers gross interest expense more than ten times, comfortably above the sector median and improved from the prior year, reflecting strong earnings power from the electrophysiology-led sales growth described in the MD&A.

Free cash flow to debt exceeds the sector median and rose year over year, as operating cash flow of four and a half billion comfortably funded capital expenditure, leaving substantial internal liquidity for debt service and acquisitions.

key_risks.text: The risk factors flag intense competition and rapid technological change, including low-cost alternatives and AI-enabled rivals, which could erode the innovation-driven sales momentum and pressure the operating margin that underpins coverage.

The debt note shows a large senior note maturing in the near term and a heavy cluster of maturities thereafter, so refinancing depends on continued access to capital markets despite the undrawn revolving facility extended to a later date.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Gross leverage sits below the sector median and declined from the prior year, while net leverage remains modestly above the sector median on a net-of-cash basis, indicating the debt load is manageable but not a standout strength.

Cash flow to debt exceeds the sector median and improved year over year, and the indicative risk profile places leverage and cash flow in the strongest tier with limited headroom to the next leverage boundary.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer presents a modest indicative financial risk profile: leverage below the sector median, coverage well above peers, and free cash flow to debt above the sector median, supported by double-digit organic sales growth in electrophysiology per the MD&A.

Analyst judgement: the credit should remain stable absent large debt-funded acquisitions, since acquisition spending already absorbs a meaningful share of free cash flow and the maturity ladder concentrates refinancing needs in the medium term.

credit_strengths.text: 經營收入覆蓋總利息支出超過十倍，遠高於行業中位數，並較上一年度有所改善，反映管理層討論與分析所述由電生理主導的銷售增長所帶來的強勁盈利能力。
自由現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，並按年上升，因經營現金流達四十五億元，足以充裕地支持資本開支，為償債及收購留下大量內部流動性。

key_risks.text: 風險因素指出競爭激烈及技術快速變革，包括低成本替代品及人工智能驅動的競爭對手，可能削弱創新驅動的銷售勢頭，並對支撐覆蓋率的經營利潤率構成壓力。
債務附註顯示一筆大額優先票據於短期內到期，其後尚有大量票據集中到期，故再融資取決於能否持續進入資本市場，儘管未提取的循環融資額度已延長至較後日期。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 總槓桿低於行業中位數，並較上一年度下降，而淨槓桿在扣除現金基礎上仍略高於行業中位數，顯示債務負擔可控，但並非突出優勢。
現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，並按年改善，而指示性風險狀況將槓桿及現金流置於最強級別，距下一槓桿界限的緩衝有限。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人呈現溫和的指示性財務風險狀況：槓桿低於行業中位數，覆蓋率遠高於同業，自由現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，並獲管理層討論與分析所述電生理業務雙位數內生銷售增長支持。
分析師判斷：在沒有大規模債務融資收購的情況下，信貸應保持穩定，因收購支出已佔用相當比例的自由現金流，而到期結構使再融資需求集中於中期。
